DECISION_REASON: State KEPT, icon REMOVED. The gauge dial is the weakest asset in the plan on two counts. (1) Grammar: a circular dial with a needle and a tick is a stock infographic pictogram; nothing resembling it exists in 448 corpus assets, and the corpus's own instrument idiom is a drawn ruler or scale, not a dial. (2) Guardrail: a needle resting at a position on a dial reads as a reading, and a tick mark reads as a threshold. The narration gives no value, no direction and no threshold - it says only that blood pressure has something to do with it. An icon that implies a measured position overclaims. Directional alternatives were considered and rejected for the same reason: an up-arrow beside BLOOD PRESSURE would assert that coffee raises it, which the narration never says. The plate therefore carries text only. Cost: the three plates become asymmetric (one text-only, two with icons). The reviewer's alternative is to drop the icons from all three plates for symmetry; that is recorded in the self-audit, not applied, because the heart and cup icons are both reuses of already-established shapes and earn their place.
